venues.name: Scientific Reports (Nature Portfolio) - TIER A journal, recommended primary target if APC funding exists
venues.fit: Strong fit and the most natural home: MedMNIST+ (Doerrich et al., Sci Rep 15:7669, 2025) and MedNet (Ferdous et al., Sci Rep 15:41936, 2025) were published here and both report DermaMNIST numbers, so editors and referees already know the benchmark. Acceptance criterion is 'original, technically sound, conclusions supported by data' (no novelty bar), which suits a careful benchmark-improvement + evaluation-protocol paper. SCIE, JCR IF ~3.8-3.9 (verify current JCR), fully open access (CC BY), counts at essentially every Indian institute. Risks: APC is unaffordable without funding (automatic waivers apply only to the world's lowest-income countries; India is not eligible; check whether the institute has a Springer Nature read-and-publish agreement). Referees are often from the biomedical side, so CLAIM/TRIPOD+AI adherence, CIs, calibration and an honest leakage discussion matter more than architecture detail. Comparable Nature Portfolio outlet for a pure dataset/benchmark-audit paper would be Scientific Data (where Abhishek et al. 2025 appeared), but that requires a data descriptor, not a model paper.
venues.format: Word or LaTeX (no .bib files accepted: references must be embedded; Nature numbered style, NOT IEEE). No strict word/page limits, but recommended: <=11 typeset pages, main text <=4,500 words (excluding abstract, Methods, references, legends), title <=20 words, abstract <=200 words with no citations, <=6 keywords, <=60 references (not strictly enforced), figure legends <=350 words, display items commensurate with length (~8 for a full Article). Section order is Introduction - Results - Discussion - Methods (Methods last, no word limit). Mandatory: Data Availability Statement (before references), Competing Interests statement, Author Contributions, Ethics declarations in Methods for human data, Supplementary Information as separate files. OA cost: APC approx. GBP 2,290 / USD 2,850 / EUR 2,490 plus taxes (DOAJ listing and a 2026 third-party check; the official Nature fee page was cookie-gated, so confirm there before budgeting). Review time: Nature Portfolio's own metrics (as relayed by secondary sources) give a median ~12 days to first editorial decision (includes desk rejections) and PubMed-derived medians of ~4 months submission-to-acceptance; plan 4-8 months to publication.

venues.name: IEEE Access - TIER A/B journal, fastest OA route
venues.fit: Good fit for an applied deep-learning paper with exhaustive experiments and ablations; multidisciplinary, SCIE-indexed (JCR IF 3.4-4.2 depending on year; a 2025-JCR value of 4.2 is reported by aggregators - verify). Peer review is binary: Accept (minor edits) / Reject with ONE resubmission permitted / Reject - so the manuscript must be complete and polished at first submission, and a weak or vague contribution statement is a common desk-reject reason. Reputation caveat: it is a mega-journal; some institutes and reviewers discount it, but it is accepted for most DDP/thesis requirements - check the institute's venue list. India is not eligible for the low-income-country discount; the corresponding author gets 5% off as an IEEE member (20% with an IEEE Society membership; student members are not eligible). Discloses AI-writing-assistance in acknowledgements.
venues.format: Mandatory IEEE Access double-column template (Word 'Access-Template-2024.docx' or the LaTeX zip, IEEEtran-derived), IEEE numbered reference style, 3-10 keywords (index terms), author biographies and photos required after the references, ORCID required for the submitting author, source file + PDF. No page limit and no over-length charge, but strongly recommended under 20 pages (longer papers need justification or a pre-submission enquiry). Conference-paper overlap must be <35% and disclosed. OA cost: APC USD 2,160 per article plus local taxes (official 2026 page). Time: the journal advertises 4-6 weeks submission-to-publication; realistically 1-3 months including one resubmission round.

venues.name: Computers in Biology and Medicine (Elsevier) - TIER A journal, recommended if no APC budget (subscription route is free)
venues.fit: Best subject fit among Elsevier titles: deep-learning medical image classification is core scope, and MedViT (Manzari et al., CBM 2023), which benchmarked on MedMNIST including DermaMNIST, appeared here. JCR Q1, IF ~6.3-7.0 (aggregators disagree; verify in JCR). Hybrid journal: publishing via the subscription route costs nothing; gold OA is optional. Very high submission volume, so desk rejection is common unless the paper has a crisp methodological framing (resolution/upsampling study + leakage-aware evaluation protocol + class-imbalance decision rule) and a clinical-interpretation paragraph. Reviewers come from both CS and biomedical engineering and routinely ask for CIs, statistical tests, calibration, external/leak-free testing and a comparison table under equal protocol. Same-family fallbacks: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine (median ~5 months to acceptance per PubMed-based aggregator) and Artificial Intelligence in Medicine.
venues.format: Elsevier 'Your Paper Your Way' at first submission (any readable format), elsarticle LaTeX template (elsarticle-num numbered references) for revision; no hard length limit (typical 7,000-10,000 words all-in; keep figures <= ~10); 3-5 Highlights (<=85 characters each), optional graphical abstract, CRediT author statement, Declaration of competing interests, Data availability statement, funding statement, and (new Elsevier policy) declaration of generative-AI use in writing. OA cost: USD 0 via subscription; gold OA APC indicative ~USD 2,600-3,100 (aggregator figure ~USD 2,610; ScienceDirect blocked automated access, so verify on Elsevier's APC price list). Review time: official Journal Insights not retrievable; aggregators indicate first decisions (incl. desk rejects) within ~1-2 weeks and ~3-5 months to acceptance.

venues.name: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control (Elsevier) - TIER B journal, fallback after CBM
venues.fit: Scope explicitly welcomes practical, applications-led biomedical image and signal analysis for diagnosis; skin-lesion classification papers are common. JCR Q1/Q2, IF ~4.9 (verify). Hybrid (free via subscription). Reviewer bar is somewhat lower than CBM but still expects statistical rigour and SOTA comparison; a good fallback if CBM desk-rejects. Less visibility in the medical-imaging ML community than MIDL/MELBA.
venues.format: elsarticle template, numbered references; no hard limit (typical 6,000-9,000 words); Highlights, CRediT, Declaration of competing interests, Data availability statement. OA cost: USD 0 via subscription; gold OA APC indicative ~USD 2,590 (aggregator; verify). Review time: aggregators report ~3 months average peer review and ~4-6 months to acceptance; no official first-decision figure retrievable.

venues.name: Expert Systems with Applications (Elsevier) - TIER B journal, only with an 'intelligent decision-support system' framing
venues.fit: High-impact (JCR IF 7.5 in the 2024 release; one aggregator cites 9.4 for the 2025 release - verify) and publishes many medical image classification papers, but scope demands an expert/intelligent-system contribution (frame the validated ensemble + TTA + logit-adjusted decision rule as a decision-support system with a reproducible evaluation protocol). Hybrid. Known for very uneven handling: fast desk decisions, but community reports of 6-17 months in review; high desk-reject rate. Choose only if the professor has prior experience with ESWA.
venues.format: elsarticle template, numbered references; concise manuscripts expected (ESWA asks authors to justify length beyond ~40 double-spaced pages incl. figures); Highlights required; CRediT; Declaration of competing interests; Data availability. OA cost: USD 0 via subscription; gold OA APC indicative ~USD 3,220-3,630 (aggregators; verify). Review time (aggregated from Elsevier insights by third parties): ~5-7 days to first (mostly desk) decision, ~60-100 days decision after review, ~150-190 days to acceptance; outliers of a year or more are reported.

venues.name: ISIC Skin Image Analysis Workshop @ MICCAI (Springer LNCS) - TIER A workshop, most exact audience; next edition expected with MICCAI 2027
venues.fit: The one venue whose entire audience is skin-lesion ML; HAM10000 is the ISIC 2018 training set and the organisers/reviewers know the DermaMNIST leakage literature (Abhishek et al.), so a leakage-aware, resolution-aware benchmark paper with honest numbers is on-topic (CFP topics include class-imbalance methods, uncertainty, robustness, fairness). Best Paper and Honorable Mention awards. 11th edition (Strasbourg, 27 Sep 2026) is over: its deadline was 10 Jul 2026 (notification 7 Aug, camera-ready 14 Aug). A 12th edition is expected alongside MICCAI 2027 in Auckland, New Zealand (27 Sep - 1 Oct 2027): expect the CFP around April 2027 and a deadline in late June/early July 2027. Costs: no APC (LNCS), but MICCAI workshop registration (several hundred USD/EUR) plus travel to New Zealand; MICCAI student travel awards exist; at least one author must present. A workshop paper can later be extended (>=35-50% new material, disclosed) into the journal version.
venues.format: MICCAI/Springer LNCS template (llncs, splncs04 references), up to 8 pages of text, figures and tables plus up to 2 pages of references; double-blind; OpenReview; supplementary material allowed; proceedings in an LNCS 'MICCAI Workshops' volume.

venues.name: MIDL 2027 (Medical Imaging with Deep Learning), Porto, 14-16 July 2027 - TIER A conference, free open-access proceedings
venues.fit: The methods-and-validation community for medical imaging ML; PMLR proceedings are free and well cited. Full-paper deadline is imminent (abstract registration 30 Nov 2026, paper 4 Dec 2026, notification 12 Feb 2027, camera-ready 12 Mar 2027) - feasible only if the 224-px model and all tables already exist; the main track expects a methodological contribution, while the 'Clinical Translation & Validation' special track explicitly does not require methodological novelty and could take the evaluation-protocol angle if framed as validation. The 3-page short-paper track (deadline TBD, historically March-April; not in PMLR) is a realistic early target for a preliminary result and reviewer feedback. Review is single-blind. At least one author must register and present in person (travel to Portugal).
venues.format: Official MIDL 2027 LaTeX template (PMLR style; fonts/margins fixed). Main track: 10 pages at submission, 12 after rebuttal, excluding references/acknowledgements/appendices; CTV track 14 (16) pages; short papers 3 pages, no appendix. OpenReview (institutional e-mail accounts avoid moderation delays). Preprints allowed; dual submission to another archival venue not allowed. No APC; registration fee + travel.

venues.name: IEEE EMBC 2027, Singapore, 11-15 July 2027 - TIER B conference
venues.fit: Large biomedical-engineering conference with IEEE Xplore and PubMed/MEDLINE indexing; historically generous acceptance, so a reliable first peer-reviewed publication and a good line for placements. Depth is limited: 4 pages fit the dataset table, main results table, one ablation and the confusion matrix only, so keep the journal version as the main vehicle (overlap must be disclosed). Full contributed papers: deadline 24 Jan 2027 (hard, AoE), notification 16 Apr 2027, final 30 Apr 2027. Costs: registration (several hundred USD; verify on the 2027 site when it opens in March 2027) plus travel; no APC.
venues.format: IEEE conference two-column template (A4/US Letter per template); 4 pages of technical content plus a 5th page containing only references (maximum 20 references); strict automated compliance check of margins, headers, page size; 1-page poster abstracts (deadline 23 Apr 2027) are NOT indexed.

venues.name: ICVGIP (Indian Conference on Computer Vision, Graphics and Image Processing) - TIER B Indian conference; 2027 edition expected
venues.fit: India's main computer-vision conference (ACM ICPS proceedings, double-blind, rebuttal phase), affordable and travel-light, and medical imaging papers are regularly accepted - good for a first peer-reviewed presentation and feedback, less international visibility than MIDL/ISIC. The 2026 edition (IIT Kharagpur Research Park / ISI Kolkata, 21-24 Dec 2026) closed on 21 Aug 2026 (notification 16 Oct, camera-ready 25 Oct); expect the 2027 CFP around May-June 2027 with a July-August 2027 deadline. Fees (2026): students INR 7,000-9,000, academics INR 12,000-14,000 (incl. GST); ACM ICPS APC may apply unless the institute is in ACM Open/ONOS or the organisers waive it (the 2026 organisers were working to waive it).
venues.format: 8 pages including text, figures and tables; references may exceed the limit; official (ACM-style) LaTeX template strongly preferred, Word allowed; PDF <=20 MB; double-blind (no names, affiliations or acknowledgements); <=20% overlap with prior/concurrent work; arXiv preprints eligible.

venues.name: MELBA (Machine Learning for Biomedical Imaging) - TIER A/B journal, free, arXiv overlay
venues.fit: Community-run journal from the MICCAI/MIDL community; free to publish, rigorous (editor screening, then 3 anonymous reviewers; Accept / Major Revisions / Reject), accepts significantly extended conference papers, and suits a thorough ~20-page benchmark + evaluation-protocol study. Caveat: no JCR impact factor and not SCIE-indexed, so it may not satisfy an institute's 'SCI journal' requirement - check before choosing. Review timeline not published; expect several months.
venues.format: Mandatory MELBA LaTeX template (text and bibliography), approximately 20 pages expected (no strict limit), submission via Scholastica, final accepted version hosted on arXiv with the MELBA template; prior arXiv posting encouraged; no fee stated.

venues.name: Medical Image Analysis (Elsevier) - NOT recommended for this paper (too ambitious); same verdict for IEEE TMI and, slightly less so, IEEE JBHI
venues.fit: Flagship methods journal (JCR IF ~10.7-10.9) that expects substantial methodological novelty or large multi-centre clinical validation; a validation-tuned ensemble with TTA and logit adjustment on a 7,007-image benchmark would almost certainly be desk-rejected regardless of the accuracy reached. PubMed-derived median submission-to-acceptance is ~262 days (IQR ~167-397). Hybrid; indicative gold-OA APC ~USD 3,970. Keep it in the related-work reading list, not the submission list.
venues.format: elsarticle template, numbered references, no fixed length, CRediT, declarations, Highlights.

structure: RECOMMENDED PATH (given the venues above): post on arXiv (cs.CV, cross-list eess.IV) on the day of journal submission; primary journal = Scientific Reports if APC funding/agreement exists, otherwise Computers in Biology and Medicine via the free subscription route (fallback BSPC); optional fast peer-reviewed companion = MIDL 2027 short paper (3 pp, deadline TBD ~spring 2027) or ISIC-SIAW 2027 (8+2 pp, deadline ~June/July 2027), with the journal paper carrying >=35-50% new material and the overlap disclosed in the cover letter.

TITLE (<=20 words, Sci Rep; <=15 is better): a declarative noun phrase stating object + dataset + key finding or protocol, no hype words, no colon-chains. Pattern: 'Resolution-aware ensembles and leakage-aware evaluation for seven-class dermoscopic classification on DermaMNIST'. Avoid 'novel', 'robust', 'efficient', 'framework', 'towards', and avoid numbers in the title unless they are the finding.

ABSTRACT (~250 words for IEEE/Elsevier; <=200 for Sci Rep; unstructured single paragraph, no citations, no undefined acronyms except AI/CNN): (1) one sentence of clinical/benchmark context; (2) one sentence stating the gap (reported DermaMNIST results mix resolutions, upsampling and splits, 13.5% of lesions appear in more than one partition, no study reports balanced accuracy or calibration); (3) 2-3 sentences of what was done (data 7,007/1,003/2,005 official split at 224 px plus DermaMNIST-C/-E, backbones, ensemble selection on the tuning split only, 8-view TTA, logit-adjusted decision rule, 3 seeds); (4) 2-3 sentences of results WITH numbers and uncertainty: top-1 accuracy, macro-AUC, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, each with 95% CI or mean +/- SD, the gain over the best single member and over the reproduced ResNet-18/DenseNet-121 baselines, and the leak-free (-E) figure; (5) one sentence of conclusion scoped to what was shown, plus code/weights/probabilities release. Follow TRIPOD+AI-for-Abstracts (13 items): data source, outcome, sample sizes per split, model type, performance measures with CIs, availability.

KEYWORDS (5-6, Sci Rep allows up to 6; IEEE 3-10 index terms): dermoscopy; skin lesion classification; DermaMNIST / MedMNIST+; HAM10000; convolutional neural network ensemble; class imbalance / logit adjustment; test-time augmentation; data leakage. Pick terms that readers search for, not ones already in the title.

1. INTRODUCTION (600-900 words; 4-6 paragraphs): P1 clinical motivation in two sentences with primary citations (Esteva 2017; Tschandl 2018) - no melanoma-statistics padding. P2 the benchmark: MedMNIST v2/MedMNIST+ DermaMNIST, why it is used (standardised split, lightweight, multi-resolution) and what the published ceilings are (DenseNet-121@224 84.74 +/- 0.51; ResNet-18@224 82.33; DINO linear probe@224 84.42), stated with resolution and protocol. P3 the gap, stated as verifiable problems: heterogeneous resolution/upsampling protocols, lesion-level leakage across partitions (1,006 of 7,470 lesions; 886 train-test images), only ACC/AUC reported, no balanced accuracy, no calibration, no seeds/CIs in several >80% reports, unverified preprint claims (DINOv2 92.02). P4 what this paper does, in one paragraph. P5 CONTRIBUTIONS LIST of 3-5 bullets, each a verifiable deliverable with its measurement, e.g. (i) a controlled study of input resolution and upsampling for five EfficientNet/V2 backbones under one protocol; (ii) a validation-selected ensemble with TTA and a logit-adjusted decision rule reaching X% top-1 / Y balanced accuracy / Z macro-AUC on the official 2,005-image test split (95% CI), vs best published a%; (iii) the first DermaMNIST results reporting balanced accuracy, per-class metrics and calibration, and a leakage-aware evaluation on DermaMNIST-C and -E; (iv) release of code, weights and per-image test probabilities so every number is recomputable. Optional final sentence on paper organisation (omit for Sci Rep).

2. RELATED WORK (500-800 words; 3-4 themed subsections, not a list of papers): 2.1 Skin-lesion classification on HAM10000/ISIC (full-resolution literature, ISIC challenge results, what accuracy ranges are typical); 2.2 DermaMNIST benchmarks (MedMNIST v2, MedMNIST+ across 28/64/128/224, MedViT, MedNet, Kadric et al.) with a compact TABLE listing resolution, upsampled-or-native, split, seeds and metric for each - this table is where protocol differences become visible; 2.3 Dataset quality and leakage (Abhishek et al. 2025: -C and -E, 'benchmarks should not be compared'); 2.4 Techniques used (ensembling, TTA aggregation, logit adjustment/long-tail learning, label smoothing, mixup, focal loss) each with one sentence of what it does and why it is relevant to a 7-class imbalanced problem. End with one paragraph positioning this work relative to each theme.

3. MATERIALS AND METHODS (1,200-1,800 words + tables; in Sci Rep this section is 'Methods' and goes LAST, after Discussion; IEEE/Elsevier keep IMRaD order): 3.1 Dataset - source (HAM10000 10,015 images, 7,470 lesions, 7 classes akiec/bcc/bkl/df/mel/nv/vasc), MedMNIST v2 split 7,007/1,003/2,005 with class counts per split (TABLE 1), MedMNIST+ files used (dermamnist_224.npz from Zenodo 10519652; MD5s), licence CC BY-NC 4.0, leakage statistics, DermaMNIST-C (8,215/573/1,227, lesion-disjoint) and -E (10,015 train; ISIC-2018 val/test 193/1,511) from Zenodo 12739457, and a FLOW DIAGRAM of images/lesions through partitions. 3.2 Pre-processing and augmentation (resizing/upsampling method and interpolation, normalisation statistics, exact augmentation list with probabilities). 3.3 Models (backbones, pretraining source, parameter counts, input sizes, classifier head). 3.4 Training protocol (loss, label smoothing, optimiser, LR schedule, epochs, batch size, early stopping criterion, mixed precision, seeds, hardware: Colab Tesla T4 16 GB, wall-clock per run). 3.5 Model selection and ensembling (what was tuned on the 1,003-image tuning split: member selection, averaging weights, TTA views; state explicitly that the test split was used once per final configuration). 3.6 Decision rule (logit adjustment formula with tau, how tau was chosen on the tuning split, and why: balanced accuracy objective). 3.7 Evaluation metrics and statistical analysis (top-1, top-3, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, macro one-vs-rest AUC, per-class sensitivity/specificity, ECE/Brier/NLL; 95% bootstrap CIs with 2,000 resamples over test images; paired comparison via McNemar or paired bootstrap of accuracy differences; mean +/- SD over >=3 seeds; Bonferroni/Holm if many comparisons). 3.8 Baselines reproduced under the identical protocol (ResNet-18@224, DenseNet-121@224 at minimum) and the exact published numbers compared against. 3.9 Implementation and reproducibility (framework versions, timm model ids, code/weights/probability-file release).

4. EXPERIMENTAL SETUP (can be merged into 3 for journals; separate in conference papers): hardware/compute budget table (GPU-hours per member, total; params; GFLOPs; inference latency per image with and without TTA), hyperparameter search space and how many configurations were tried (reviewers read 'we tried 40 configurations and report the best on test' as leakage - show that selection used the tuning split), and random-seed policy.

5. RESULTS (1,000-1,500 words; observations only, no interpretation; every number with CI): 5.1 Main results table on the official test split (single members, plain average, weighted average, +TTA, +logit adjustment; columns ACC, bACC, macro-F1, macro-AUC, top-3, ECE) with tuning-split columns alongside to expose the val-test gap. 5.2 Comparison with published results under declared protocol (table with resolution/upsampling/seeds; separate block for 'reported, not independently reproduced' preprints). 5.3 Per-class performance table and confusion matrix, with explicit text on melanoma sensitivity and the minority classes (df, vasc, akiec). 5.4 ROC/PR curves and calibration (reliability diagram; ECE before/after). 5.5 Leakage-aware evaluation: the same frozen model(s) retrained/evaluated on DermaMNIST-C and -E, side by side with Abhishek et al.'s ResNet-18 numbers; state that -C and original numbers are not comparable. 5.6 Ablations (resolution 64->96/112/128/224; backbone; loss; mixup/label smoothing; ensemble size k; number of TTA views; decision rule) each as a difference with CI. 5.7 Failure analysis: most frequent confusions, examples (with licence attribution), and effect of the decision rule on nv-vs-minority trade-off. Statistical significance statements only where a test was run and named.

6. DISCUSSION (700-1,000 words): P1 restate the principal finding in one sentence with numbers. P2 what explains the gain (resolution, ensembling, TTA, decision rule) with reference to the ablations, and what did not help. P3 relation to published results, including why MedMNIST+ EfficientNet-B4 underperforms and how our protocol differs; treat the 92% preprint explicitly and neutrally. P4 clinical/practical meaning stated cautiously (7-class dermoscopic triage support, not diagnosis; dataset is dermoscopy from two sites; no skin-tone metadata). P5 LIMITATIONS as its own subsection (see style rule 9): leakage in the official split and what -E shows; small test set (2,005) and CI width; validation-tuned decision rule risk; compute budget limiting 224-px training; no external prospective data; no reader study; licence restricts commercial use; HAM10000 lacks Fitzpatrick/skin-tone labels so fairness cannot be evaluated. P6 future work tied to specific limitations (lesion-level cross-validation, ISIC 2019/2020 external test, calibration under shift).

7. CONCLUSION (120-200 words): what was done, the headline numbers with CIs, the protocol recommendation (report resolution/upsampling, seeds, balanced accuracy, calibration, and -E results), and the released artefacts. No new results, no citations, no hype.

DECLARATIONS BLOCK (order varies by venue; Sci Rep puts Data Availability before references and ethics in Methods; Elsevier uses CRediT + Declaration of competing interests + Data availability + Funding + AI declaration; IEEE puts funding in the first-page footnote and biographies after references): Data availability; Code availability; Ethics statement (secondary use of public de-identified data); Author contributions (CRediT); Competing interests; Funding; Acknowledgements (dataset creators, Colab compute, anyone who helped but is not an author); Generative-AI use disclosure; Reporting-checklist statement (CLAIM 2024 completed in Supplementary); Preprint statement. Templates are in the 'statements' list.

REFERENCES: use the venue's style - IEEE numbered style for IEEE Access/EMBC ([n] A. B. Author, C. Author, and D. Author, 'Title in sentence case,' Journal Abbrev., vol. 15, no. 1, pp. 1-10, Mon. 2025, doi: 10.xxxx; conference: 'Title,' in Proc. Conf. Abbrev., City, Country, 2021, pp. 1-10; preprint: 'Title,' 2025, arXiv:2501.14685 (version and 'under review' noted in text, not in the reference); dataset: Tschandl et al., Sci Data 5, 180161 (2018) plus Zenodo DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.10519652 and 10.5281/zenodo.12739457 with access dates); Nature numbered style for Sci Rep (no .bib, embedded); elsarticle-num for Elsevier; splncs04 for LNCS. Cite primary sources (ICML/ICLR/CVPR papers, Sci Data, Sci Rep), never blogs or Wikipedia; include DOIs; 40-60 references for a journal paper, <=20 for EMBC; every claim in Related Work has a citation; do not cite papers you have not read.

SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: full hyperparameter tables per member; per-seed results; extended ablations; additional ROC/PR/reliability plots; the completed CLAIM 2024 checklist (44 items) and TRIPOD+AI checklist (27 items) with page/line references; the leakage audit (how overlaps were counted); the exact commands/config files to regenerate every table from the released probability files.

LENGTH BUDGETS: Sci Rep ~4,500 words main text (Intro+Results+Discussion) + unlimited Methods, ~8 display items; IEEE Access 12-18 typeset pages; CBM/BSPC/ESWA ~8,000-10,000 words all-in with <=10 figures/tables; ISIC-SIAW 8 pages + 2 references; MIDL 10 (+2) pages excl. refs; EMBC 4 pages + references; ICVGIP 8 pages + references.
checklists: WHICH CHECKLIST TO USE: this is a medical-imaging AI model development-and-internal-testing study, so CLAIM 2024 is the primary checklist (complete it item by item and submit it as a supplement; cite it in Methods). Use TRIPOD+AI as a second self-audit because many biomedical referees reach for it (and its abstract checklist shapes the abstract). STARD-AI applies only if the paper is framed as a diagnostic-test-accuracy study of a fixed classifier; cite it as context. MI-CLAIM is older but its reproducibility tiers are a crisp way to state what is released. Mention in the Methods: 'This report follows the CLAIM 2024 checklist (Supplementary Table S1) and TRIPOD+AI where applicable.'

CLAIM 2024 - Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: 2024 Update (Tejani AS, Klontzas ME, Gatti AA, et al.; Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2024;6(4):e240300; doi:10.1148/ryai.240300; 44 items answered Yes/No/Not Applicable with page/line numbers). Sections: Title/Abstract (1-2), Introduction (3-4), Methods (5-34: study design, data, reference standard, data partitions, testing data, model, training, evaluation), Results (35-39: data, model performance), Discussion (40-41), Other information (42-44). Terminology the panel enforces: say 'reference standard' (not ground truth/gold standard) and 'internal testing set' / 'external testing set' (not 'validation set'; MedMNIST's 'val' should be introduced as the tuning split). New item 13 asks for the image acquisition protocol (dermoscopes/cameras of HAM10000 per Tschandl et al.). Items that bite for this project: data source and eligibility, de-identification, how partitions were formed and whether they are disjoint at the LESION level (they are not in the official split - say so and quantify), number of images per partition and per class, pretraining source, hyperparameter search method and the data it used, augmentation, ensembling method, performance metrics with CIs, statistical tests, calibration, failure analysis, flow diagram, external testing (DermaMNIST-E serves as the closest leak-free test), code/weights availability, and limitations.

TRIPOD+AI - Collins GS, Moons KGM, Dhiman P, et al. BMJ 2024;385:e078378 (27 items / 52 sub-items; replaces TRIPOD 2015; separate 13-item TRIPOD+AI for Abstracts; checklists at tripod-statement.org). Items most relevant here: 5a data sources and representativeness; 7 data pre-processing (and whether equal across groups); 10 sample-size justification (state that the split is fixed by the benchmark and report CI width as the consequence); 12a how data were partitioned; 12c model type, all model-building steps incl. hyperparameter tuning and method for internal validation; 12e all performance measures and plots and their rationale (discrimination, calibration); 13 CLASS IMBALANCE methods and any subsequent recalibration - this item is exactly our logit-adjusted decision rule, so document why/how and its calibration effect; 14 fairness approaches (state none possible: no skin-tone metadata); 15 model output and how thresholds/decision rules were identified; 16 differences between development and evaluation data (original vs -C vs -E); 17 ethical approval; 18a-f funding, conflicts, protocol, registration (state 'not registered'), data sharing, code sharing; 20b characteristics table per split; 21 numbers in each analysis; 22 full model specification (release weights so third parties can evaluate); 23a performance with CIs incl. subgroups (per class); 25 interpretation incl. fairness; 26 limitations with their effect on bias and generalisability; 27c next steps.

STARD-AI - The STARD-AI reporting guideline for diagnostic accuracy studies using artificial intelligence (Sounderajah V, Guni A, Liu X, Collins GS, ... Darzi A, Ashrafian H; Nature Medicine 2025;31:3283-3289; doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03953-8). 40 items: title/abstract (1), abstract (2), introduction (3-4), methods (5-23: study design, ethics, participants, dataset, test methods, analysis), results (24-32), discussion (33-35), other information (36-40). Four STARD 2015 items modified (1, 3, 7, 25) and fourteen new AI items (6, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15b, 15d, 23, 28, 29, 35, 39, 40a, 40b): dataset- and participant-level eligibility (7), data source and collection (11), annotation process (12), capture devices and software versions (13), acquisition protocol and pre-processing (14), partitioning into training/tuning/test (15b), test-set characteristics (25), representativeness of the target condition in the test set (28), commercial interests (39), public availability of data and code (40a), external audit/evaluation of outputs (40b). A participant/image flow diagram is expected (item 24). The paper itself says CLAIM is the better fit for developing/validating an imaging model and STARD-AI for diagnostic-accuracy-focused studies.

MI-CLAIM - Minimum information about clinical artificial intelligence modeling (Norgeot B, Quer G, Beaulieu-Jones BK, ... Butte AJ; Nature Medicine 2020;26(9):1320-1324; doi:10.1038/s41591-020-1041-y). Six parts: (1) study design (clinical setting, population, state-of-the-art baselines); (2) data and partitioning (train/tuning/test with no leakage - state the lesion-level leakage of the official split and how -C/-E address it); (3) optimisation and final model selection (all tuning on the tuning split; final model fixed before the single test evaluation); (4) performance evaluation (primary metric chosen a priori, CIs, calibration, subgroup/per-class results); (5) model examination (saliency/failure cases; check for bias and shortcut features); (6) reproducibility tiers - Tier 1 full code + data release, Tier 2 third-party evaluation of code, Tier 3 release of a runnable model/binary, Tier 4 no release. Because DermaMNIST is public, aim for Tier 1 and say so explicitly: code, trained weights, configs and per-image probability files. A 2024 generative-AI extension (MI-CLAIM-GEN, arXiv:2403.02558) is not applicable here.

OTHER INSTRUMENTS REVIEWERS MAY APPLY: PROBAST+AI (Moons KGM et al., BMJ 2025;388:e082505) - risk-of-bias/applicability tool with 16 development and 18 evaluation signalling questions (data partitioning and leakage, sample size, handling of class imbalance, overfitting/optimism, calibration reported, test set representative) - write Methods so each question can be answered 'low risk'. FUTURE-AI (Lekadir K et al., BMJ 2025;388:e081554) - six principles (fairness, universality, traceability, usability, robustness, explainability) and 30 best practices; cite only if the Discussion claims trustworthiness, and then map one sentence per principle. Model Cards (Mitchell et al., FAT* 2019) and Datasheets for Datasets (Gebru et al., CACM 2021): ship a model card with the weights (intended use: research on dermoscopic 7-class classification; out-of-scope: clinical use, non-dermoscopic photos; licence CC BY-NC 4.0 inherited). ML reproducibility checklist (Pineau et al., JMLR 2021): seeds, compute, number of runs, hyperparameter search budget.

PROJECT-SPECIFIC PRE-SUBMISSION AUDIT (what 'survives peer review' means here): (1) every number in every table/figure is regenerated by one script from saved per-image probability files for each split, seed and configuration - keep the files with the paper and release them; (2) the official test split is evaluated once per FINAL configuration; all selection (members, weights, TTA views, tau) is on the 1,003-image tuning split and this sentence appears verbatim in Methods; (3) >=3 seeds for every reported configuration, mean +/- SD, plus 95% bootstrap CIs on the test set (2,000 resamples), plus paired tests for headline comparisons; (4) report tuning-split and test-split numbers side by side (the val-test gap is the overfitting evidence reviewers want); (5) reproduce at least two published baselines (ResNet-18@224, DenseNet-121@224) under your protocol instead of only copying numbers; (6) a comparison table whose columns include resolution, native vs upsampled, split, seeds, source; (7) quote the leakage statistics (1,006 of 7,470 lesions in >1 partition; train-test 886 images / 641 lesions) with citation and evaluate on DermaMNIST-C and -E; never write 'accuracy drops by X after de-leaking' (C goes up, E goes down); (8) cite the Wu & Papiez 92.02% as 'reported in a preprint under review, not independently reproduced' and do not claim to beat or trail it; (9) correct the earlier auto-sklearn error (0.719 not 0.749) and audit every copied number against the source table; (10) state the dataset licence (CC BY-NC 4.0) and that released weights inherit non-commercial terms; (11) declare compute (free Colab T4) honestly - it explains why 224-px training is limited and is not a weakness to hide; (12) the paper has no sentence of the form 'to the best of our knowledge, first' unless it was verified by a literature search described in Related Work (balanced accuracy on DermaMNIST qualifies, with the search stated).
reviewer_objections: 'The official DermaMNIST split leaks lesions across partitions (Abhishek et al. 2025), so your 82-87% is inflated and not comparable.' - Pre-empt: quantify the leakage in the dataset section, report the same pipeline on DermaMNIST-C (lesion-disjoint) and DermaMNIST-E (ISIC-2018 val/test, leak-free), discuss direction of bias, and frame the official-split number as 'comparable to prior benchmark reports' rather than as clinical performance.

'You compare against MedMNIST+ numbers obtained at different resolutions/upsampling and with 3 seeds - apples to oranges.' - Pre-empt: a comparison table with protocol columns; reproduce ResNet-18 and DenseNet-121 at 224 px under your protocol; never say 'outperforms' across protocols, say 'higher than the reported value of'.

'No confidence intervals, no seeds, no significance tests; differences of 1-2 points on 2,005 images are within noise.' - Pre-empt: bootstrap CIs on every estimate, mean +/- SD over seeds, McNemar/paired bootstrap for ensemble vs best single model and vs baselines; acknowledge when a difference is not significant.

'The ensemble weights, TTA views and logit-adjustment temperature were tuned on the validation set and you report the best test number - this is test-set optimisation.' - Pre-empt: explicit selection protocol, one-shot test evaluation per final config, report val and test together, show the number of configurations tried, and include a sensitivity analysis of tau.

'Ensembling + TTA + logit adjustment is engineering, not a scientific contribution.' - Pre-empt: make the contribution the controlled study (resolution/upsampling, decision rule for imbalance, leakage-aware protocol, calibration) with ablations isolating each factor; position the paper as a benchmark-and-protocol paper, not a 'novel architecture' paper.

'Accuracy is the wrong headline for a 67%-majority-class problem.' - Pre-empt: lead with balanced accuracy and macro-F1 alongside top-1 and macro-AUC; per-class table with melanoma sensitivity/specificity; PR curves for df/vasc/akiec.

'Logit adjustment trades majority-class accuracy for minority recall - show the trade-off and the calibration consequences.' - Pre-empt: before/after per-class bars, reliability diagrams and ECE/Brier with and without the rule, and a statement that the rule is a post-hoc decision policy applied to calibrated probabilities (TRIPOD+AI item 13).

'The model is not calibrated / no uncertainty.' - Pre-empt: temperature scaling on the tuning split, reliability diagram, ECE, NLL, Brier; optional ensemble disagreement as uncertainty with a coverage-vs-accuracy curve.

'Why no external validation on ISIC 2019/2020 or a different dermoscopy source?' - Pre-empt: use DermaMNIST-E (its test is the ISIC 2018 official test, 1,511 images) as the external-ish test; list true external validation as future work with reasons (compute, licence).

'You claim state of the art but a preprint reports 92%.' - Pre-empt: cite it as reported-not-reproduced and unusually high relative to all peer-reviewed results; do not benchmark your claim against it; use 'highest peer-reviewed/independently reproducible result we are aware of under protocol X'.

'The clinical relevance is overstated: 7-class classification of 28/64/224-px crops is not diagnosis.' - Pre-empt: one measured sentence about triage/benchmarking value, explicit 'not intended for clinical use' statement in Discussion and model card, no 'dermatologist-level' language.

'Fairness: skin tone and demographics are not analysed.' - Pre-empt: state that HAM10000/DermaMNIST carry no Fitzpatrick labels and only age/sex/site in the source metadata (not in the MedMNIST files), that the data come from two sites (Austria, Australia), and name this as a limitation per TRIPOD+AI item 14 and CLAIM.

'Insufficient implementation detail / not reproducible.' - Pre-empt: timm model identifiers, pretrained weights source, exact augmentation list, LR schedule, epochs, batch size, seeds, software versions, wall-clock on T4, config files and probability files in a public repository with a DOI (Zenodo) and a model card.

'The literature review is thin / misses skin-lesion work on full-resolution HAM10000/ISIC.' - Pre-empt: a themed Related Work with the full-resolution literature and ISIC challenge results, so the DermaMNIST results are positioned as a benchmark study, not a claim about dermatology at large.

'Figures: no error bars, inconsistent class order, unreadable fonts, confusion matrix without counts.' - Pre-empt: one plotting script, fixed class order, counts + row-normalised percentages, CIs everywhere, vector PDFs, colour-blind-safe palette.

'Licence/ethics: CC BY-NC 4.0 and secondary use of patient images.' - Pre-empt: ethics statement citing the source approvals reported by Tschandl et al. 2018, a sentence that only de-identified public data were used and no new human data were collected, and a licence statement that released models inherit non-commercial terms.

'Training curves and qualitative Grad-CAM figures are filler.' - Pre-empt: put training curves in Supplementary unless they show early-stopping behaviour; include saliency only with a failure analysis and without claiming explainability.

'Overlap with your conference/workshop paper or arXiv version.' - Pre-empt: disclose in the cover letter, keep overlap below venue limits (IEEE Access <35%; ICVGIP <20% for the conference paper), and add genuinely new experiments to the journal version.
figures_tables: TABLE 1 - Dataset summary: 7 classes with full names and abbreviations (actinic keratoses/intraepithelial carcinoma akiec, basal cell carcinoma bcc, benign keratosis-like lesions bkl, dermatofibroma df, melanoma mel, melanocytic nevi nv, vascular lesions vasc), image counts and percentages per class for train/tuning/test of the official split (7,007/1,003/2,005), DermaMNIST-C (8,215/573/1,227) and DermaMNIST-E (10,015 / 193 / 1,511), source resolution 600x450 and MedMNIST+ sizes 28/64/128/224, number of unique lesions, lesion-level leakage counts (train-test 886 images / 641 lesions; 1,006 lesions in >1 partition), licence CC BY-NC 4.0, Zenodo DOIs.

FIGURE 1 - Pipeline/architecture diagram: HAM10000 -> MedMNIST+ 224 px -> pre-processing/augmentation -> five backbone members (names, input sizes, params) -> 8-view TTA -> probability averaging with tuning-split weights -> logit-adjusted decision rule -> prediction; annotate what is fixed vs tuned and on which split. Vector graphic, one colour per stage, no decorative icons.
FIGURE 2 - Representative images per class at 28, 64, 128 and 224 px (one row per class) to make the resolution argument visually; include attribution (HAM10000, CC BY-NC 4.0) in the caption.

FIGURE 3 - Flow diagram of images and lesions through partitions (CLAIM/STARD-AI expectation): HAM10000 10,015 images / 7,470 lesions -> official split with overlap arrows quantified -> -C and -E constructions; shows exactly where leakage sits.

TABLE 2 - Prior DermaMNIST results with protocol columns: method, resolution, native vs upsampled, split (original/-C/-E), seeds, ACC, AUC, balanced accuracy (blank where not reported), peer-reviewed vs preprint; rows from MedMNIST v2 (ResNet-18/50 at 28/224, AutoML), MedMNIST+ end-to-end/linear-probe at 64/128/224, MedViT, MedNet, Kadric et al., and preprints in a visually separated 'not independently reproduced' block.

TABLE 3 - Main results on the official test split: rows = each single member, plain average, tuning-weighted average, +TTA, +logit adjustment, reproduced ResNet-18@224 and DenseNet-121@224 baselines; columns = top-1, top-3, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, macro-AUC, ECE, each as mean +/- SD over seeds with 95% bootstrap CI for the final model; matching tuning-split columns (or a companion table) to show the val-test gap; bold only the best per column; footnote the exact selection protocol.

TABLE 4 - Per-class metrics for the final model (and the strongest baseline): n test images, sensitivity (recall), specificity, precision, F1, one-vs-rest AUC, each with 95% CI; highlight melanoma and the three minority classes.

FIGURE 4 - Confusion matrix of the final model on the official test split with counts and row-normalised percentages, fixed class order, colour-blind-safe sequential map; optionally a second panel for the baseline or for DermaMNIST-E.
FIGURE 5 - One-vs-rest ROC curves per class with macro-AUC and 95% CI band, plus precision-recall curves for df, vasc, akiec, mel (PR is more informative under imbalance).
FIGURE 6 - Calibration: reliability diagram(s) with ECE and Brier score for ensemble before/after temperature scaling and with/without logit adjustment; include a confidence histogram inset.

TABLE 5 - Ablations as differences from a stated reference configuration with 95% CIs: input resolution (64 -> 96/112/128/224 and native-vs-upsampled), backbone, loss (CE / label smoothing / focal), mixup, ensemble size k (1..5), number of TTA views (1/4/8), decision rule (argmax vs logit adjustment with tau sweep), pretraining; mark statistically indistinguishable rows.

FIGURE 7 - Ablation plots: accuracy and balanced accuracy vs input resolution for each backbone (lines with CI bands); accuracy vs ensemble size; balanced accuracy vs tau with the chosen tau marked (selected on the tuning split).

TABLE 6 - Leakage-aware evaluation: the same recipe trained/evaluated on official, DermaMNIST-C and DermaMNIST-E, alongside Abhishek et al.'s ResNet-18 reference rows (e.g. -C 224: 0.953 AUC / 0.847 ACC; -E 224: 0.896 / 0.685), with an explicit footnote that original and -C are not comparable.
FIGURE 8 - Per-class change in sensitivity from the logit-adjusted decision rule (paired bars, baseline vs rule) to show the nv-vs-minority trade-off honestly.

FIGURE 9 (optional, main text only if it supports a claim) - Failure analysis: most frequent confusions with example images and, if used, Grad-CAM overlays labelled as qualitative; otherwise Supplementary.

TABLE 7 - Training configuration and compute: optimiser, LR schedule, epochs, batch size, augmentations, mixed precision, seeds, GPU (Tesla T4 16 GB, Colab), wall-clock per member and total GPU-hours, parameters, GFLOPs, inference latency per image with/without TTA (may be Supplementary for Sci Rep).

SUPPLEMENTARY - training/validation curves (loss and balanced accuracy per epoch, with early-stopping epoch marked), per-seed results, full hyperparameter search space and number of trials, additional ROC/PR/reliability plots for -C/-E, completed CLAIM 2024 and TRIPOD+AI checklists with page references, model card, and the command list to regenerate every table from the released probability files.

PRESENTATION RULES: all plots from one script with one style file; fixed class order and colour per class across every figure; colour-blind-safe palettes (sequential for matrices, categorical with <=7 hues); CIs or SD on every point estimate; axis labels with units and metric definitions; fonts >=7 pt at final print size; vector PDF/EPS (raster only for images); no 3-D, no dual axes, no chart junk; tables with consistent decimals (2 for percentages, 3 for AUC), bold best, footnotes for protocol; every figure and table referenced in the text in numerical order with a self-contained caption that states dataset, split, model, n and uncertainty type.

style_rules: 1. Scope every performance claim to split, resolution, protocol and metric. Write 'The ensemble reached 82.64% top-1 accuracy (95% CI x-y) on the official 2,005-image DermaMNIST test split at 112-128 px upsampled from 64-px source data', never 'our model achieves 82.6% accuracy'. A number without its protocol is a student-report number.

2. Numbers carry uncertainty and sensible precision. Every point estimate has a 95% CI or mean +/- SD over seeds; improvements are reported as differences with CIs (and the test used); percentages to two decimals, AUC to three, never more precision than the CI width justifies; 'significant' appears only in its statistical sense with the test named, otherwise use 'larger', 'consistent', 'material'.

3. Tense discipline. Past tense for what you did and observed (Methods, Results: 'we trained', 'accuracy increased'); present tense for established facts, for definitions and for referring to the paper's own content ('Table 3 shows', 'logit adjustment rescales'); present perfect for the state of the literature ('several studies have reported'). Do not mix within a paragraph.

4. Voice. Active voice with 'we' for actions and decisions ('we selected members on the tuning split'); passive only when the agent is irrelevant ('images were resized to 224 px'); never 'the authors', 'this researcher', 'I', or anthropomorphic 'the paper argues'.

5. Delete evaluative words. Strike 'novel', 'remarkable', 'excellent', 'very', 'clearly', 'highly', 'promising', 'cutting-edge', 'robust' (unless robustness was tested), 'efficient' (unless cost was measured) and 'state-of-the-art' (unless a table shows it under equal protocol). Let the table carry the judgement.

6. Hedge in proportion to evidence, once per claim. Measured facts are stated flatly ('balanced accuracy was 66.2%'); interpretations get one calibrated hedge ('this suggests', 'is consistent with'); never stack hedges ('may possibly suggest') and never hedge a number. Use 'we did not observe' instead of 'there is no effect'.

7. Separate observation from interpretation. Results sentences describe what the data show and point to the table; interpretation, mechanisms and comparisons with literature belong in Discussion. Ban 'this proves', 'this confirms that our approach is superior'; prefer 'this indicates', 'one explanation is'.

8. Compare honestly and specifically. Compare only under matched protocol; when quoting others' numbers, state their resolution, upsampling, split and seeds in the same sentence or table; mark preprints as 'reported, not independently reproduced'; use 'higher than the reported value of 84.74% (DenseNet-121, 224 px, 3 seeds)' rather than 'outperforms all existing methods'.

9. Write limitations as specific statements with mechanism and direction of bias, each paired with what was done about it. 'Because 13.5% of lesions appear in more than one partition of the official split, accuracy on it is likely optimistic; our DermaMNIST-E result (x%) bounds this effect', not 'the dataset has some limitations'. Never let the limitations paragraph be shorter than the contributions list.

10. Contributions are verifiable deliverables. Each bullet names what was done, how it was measured and the outcome ('a controlled resolution study across five backbones showing that upsampling 64-px data to 112 px adds +1.7 points (CI ...)'), never 'we propose a novel framework' or 'we conduct extensive experiments'. Three to five bullets; the abstract, introduction and conclusion must agree on them word for word in substance.

11. Precise terminology, defined once and used consistently. 'Tuning split (MedMNIST validation set)' and 'test split' - never 'validation' alone; 'reference standard' not 'ground truth'; 'image' vs 'lesion'; 'upsampled from 64 px' not 'high resolution'; 'probability averaging' vs 'stacking'; 'balanced accuracy = mean per-class recall' defined at first use; every acronym expanded once; notation (N, C, tau, p) fixed in Methods and never reused with another meaning.

12. Paragraph and sentence craft. One idea per paragraph with the topic sentence first; sentences of about 15-30 words, no chains of 'and'; no 'as mentioned above/below', 'etc.', 'a lot', 'in order to', 'it is worth noting that', 'in this paper we ...' repeated more than once; figures and tables cited in order with self-contained captions; consistent British or American spelling; SI units and numerals with units/percent (82.64%, 224 px, 16 GB); the Conclusion introduces no new results; the Title and Abstract contain no hype and are understandable to a clinician and to an ML researcher alike.
